Related: the open-world-enforcing refusal and the no-promotion demotion are cooperative APIs, so a caller reading GG_REGISTRY_MODE directly bypasses both named refusals; the same choke point should force them.

audit-groundedness-gate: a valid but EMPTY registry (blocking_cap=0, header, zero rows) makes the canary vacuous - expected_total=1, only the baseline fixture, zero per-check mutants - so CANARY_OK would mean "baseline matched empty output" rather than "a registered check can fail". gg_canary_run should refuse a registry with zero rows as UNVERIFIED with its own reason, on the same fail-closed principle as the short/unreadable/shape-mismatch corpora.

Lane dispatch must not silently reuse a branch name. When the architect commits a codex lane worktree, check file modes first: a bash-shebang file created in the sandbox can land 100644 and turn gates-linux red, as lib/audit-call.sh did at 74d7a33. Any CI step whose job is to REPORT a failure rather than gate on one must disable errexit explicitly. GitHub runs shell: bash with -eo pipefail, so such a step is destroyed by the first failure it was written to observe, and continue-on-error hides that as non-fatal. Silence from a diagnostic step is not evidence of a clean result; a diagnostic must print something on every path. Review existing informational steps for the same shape before the tag.

audit-groundedness-gate MEDIUM from the T3 audit: an empty registry is not fail-closed. Unreadable JSON yields GG_CHECK_FIXTURE_INVALID and an unimplemented gg_check_$id yields GG_CHECK_UNIMPLEMENTED, both correct, but an empty GG_REGISTRY_IDS only triggers a reload of GG_DEFAULT_REGISTRY, and a registry that loads successfully with ZERO rows is accepted: the evaluate loop then runs zero times and returns 0, so CANARY_OK means "no checks ran" rather than "no violations found". gg_canary_run should refuse a zero-row registry with its own UNVERIFIED reason, on the same principle as the short and shape-mismatched corpora.

audit-groundedness-gate MEDIUM from the T3 audit: G1 declares repository_head among its required_inputs but its predicate tests membership in changed_paths only. gg_check_require can therefore mark G1 unevaluated when repository_head is absent, while a citation genuinely outside the diff goes unflagged - a silent under-fire relative to the declared inputs, and a contradiction of G1 own zero-false-positive rationale, which says "absent from the complete diff AND repository path sets". Either use repository_head in the predicate or remove it from required_inputs and amend the rationale.

When a script that documented itself as side-effect-free gains a mutation, re-derive its safety properties rather than editing the sentence. foreman-setup.sh changed from "mutates nothing on disk" to building a launcher; the doc was honestly updated but the four properties that purity had been providing for free - atomic replacement, a guarded test seam, parse-before-mutate, and unchanged signal coverage - were not added. Treat the removal of a purity claim as a checklist trigger, not a comment edit.

Criterion 2 requires the suite to pass on three CONSECUTIVE runs and criterion 3 requires both gates green on main. Pre-merge verification must include the two things WSL cannot show. First, file modes as recorded in the index for every new file (obligation 75, already caught one recurrence). Second, any test carrying a wall-clock or resource bound must be identified before merge and its margin stated, because a bound met locally with a small margin will fail on a slower shared runner. Both regressions today were caught by CI rather than by me, and each cost a red main plus a diagnosis cycle. Cheapest implementation: a pre-merge script that prints index modes for new files and greps the changed tests for time-based assertions.

While main is red on the canary cost overrun, every gates-linux run carries three known failures in tests/gate-ground.bats. Any NEW failure must be distinguished from those three before it is attributed to the commit under inspection. This is the exact trap that made me call a six-run red streak a one-run regression earlier today: I read the newest run rather than the first red one. Until the canary-cost fix lands, diagnose by comparing the failing test NAMES against {canary validates exact count, canary evaluates the corpus, mutation proof}, not by the pass/fail verdict.

Every scripted edit-then-commit must gate the commit on its own verification step, with a nonzero exit that stops the script. Today a checklist corruption reached origin because the script printed a verification result and then committed regardless. Pattern to use: compute the check, test it, exit 1 on failure BEFORE git add. Applies to every scratchpad script in this workflow that edits a tracked file.

AMENDS obligation 75. The pre-merge file-mode check must cover MODIFIED tracked files, not only new ones. It was written as a scan of git ls-files -o (untracked), which is where the first two exec-bit regressions came from; the third came from a lane modifying an already-tracked bash script and dropping its mode, which the merge recorded as "mode change 100755 => 100644" and the check never saw. Correct form: run bats tests/line-endings.bats before every merge and act on what it flags - it derives the inventory from a whole-repo shebang property and is exempt from nothing.

Confirm the gates-linux queue drains and yields a verdict on c251a22 or later. Seven runs sat in_progress with all steps concluded for 20+ minutes. Scripted edits to tracked files must write a temp file, assert on its contents, and os.replace it over the original - never open the target for writing directly. A python open(...,"w") that raises on a bad argument truncates the file first, which emptied tests/gate-ground.bats today; only the commit gate prevented the push. This complements obligation 83 (gate the commit on verification): the gate stops a bad commit, but write-to-temp stops the damage.

When merging any lane that ran fm-session.py, discard .foreman/session.db from the lane worktree before committing. The script creates a store wherever it runs, so a lane worktree gains an orphaned one that nothing reads; committing it would place a second divergent store in the repository. The tool already warns about this at runtime - the pre-merge routine must act on the warning.

OWNER DECISION: reword criterion 5. It requires a codex-auditor verdict per package, which cannot be satisfied for any package codex implemented without violating the cross-vendor invariant the release itself now enforces in code. Either reword to "a cross-vendor auditor verdict per package" (the vendor chosen by ac_select_auditor, recorded in the verdict), or state that codex-implemented packages are audited by grok and the criterion means the AUDIT happened rather than that a specific CLI produced it. Leaving it naming codex makes the criterion unsatisfiable by construction.

Criterion 5 needs a defined artifact before it can be counted. audit-run.sh writes audit-verdict.json per RUN, and this session audited per LANE, but nothing in the tree defines what a per-PACKAGE verdict is or where it lives. Define that artifact (path, schema, which run produced it) and then count it; until then any "N of 34 packages audited" figure is unfounded, including the 30-of-34 grep proxy I took, which only shows the package name appears somewhere under docs/evidence.

Decide what foreman does about uutils mkdir now that it is proven non-atomic. lib/lock.sh is fail-closed and correctly refuses an untrusted mechanism, so nothing is silently broken - but on a stock Ubuntu 26.04 host BOTH mechanisms fail to earn trust (mkdir non-atomic by contention, flock unknown because ptrace is denied), which leaves the lock unusable rather than merely unproven. Options: prefer GNU mkdir when gnu-coreutils is installed and pin the binary in the trust record rather than trusting the name on PATH; or license flock by a non-strace route so it can carry the lock on hosts without ptrace. The residual entry that says the alternation could not be reproduced locally should be replaced with fact 214.
